title: Universal Identifier Reuse Across Bounded Contexts
pattern: Using the exact same raw identifier primitive type to represent different business concepts across different Bounded Contexts.
why_bad: It leads to logical semantic errors. Developers can easily pass a ledger ID where a publisher ID is expected, bypassing compiler checks because both are raw `u64` primitives.
detection: Identical identifier primitives used for logically distinct, same-named entities across separate system packages.
counterexample: Unified enterprise-wide stable system identity keys (e.g. UUIDs used strictly as strings). Mark as `Context-dependent`.
source: *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (Chapter 14); *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (Chapter 3, p. 179).
